text: IN THE NEWSOctober 1, 2026Why Dark Red Utah May Be Fertile Ground for DemocratsDaily KosDaily Kos on why deep-red Utah may be fertile ground for Democrats. It cites a new poll of the 4th District, which Trump carried by 32.5 points in 2024, with Kennedy at 41% and Larsen at 33%, and says that if the polls are right, Republicans will see "a huge underperformance from 2024."Read More→

IN THE NEWSOctober 12, 2026Housing, Iran, and Public Lands Divide 4th Congressional District CandidatesUtah Public RadioUPR's recap of the Snow College debate. Larsen, a Marine combat veteran, argues that ending the Iran War would bring the quickest relief at the pump and that Kennedy gave up Congress's Article I power to declare war. He says ending "egregious tariffs" would make homes more affordable to build, and that public lands must remain in public hands to protect the ecosystem and water supplies.Read More→

IN THE NEWSOctober 12, 2026Utah Congressional District 4: U.S. Rep. Mike Kennedy Faces 3 ChallengersThe Salt Lake TribuneThe Tribune's voter guide to the 4th District race, with each candidate answering the same questions. Larsen, a Marine Corps combat veteran and self-described "Blue Dog Democrat," backs the Unrig Washington campaign to ban congressional stock trading, reject corporate PAC money and end dark money; ties the affordability crisis to the Iran War and its cost; calls for federal help converting farm irrigation to put water back into the Great Salt Lake; and says Congress should "agree better" on the 90% of issues voters share.Read More→

IN THE NEWSOctober 15, 2026Utah Congressional District 4 (“CD4”): Burt, Kennedy, Larsen, and WrightNetwork of Utah ModeratesThe Network of Utah Moderates' guide to the 4th District race. It says Larsen, a Marine veteran who grew up in a trailer park and spent time in foster care, would bring a "highly unusual and, in our opinion, helpful background to Congress," notes he is one of the few candidates talking about helping both farmers and veterans, and credits him for not criticizing voters across the aisle. The group says it cannot in good conscience recommend Kennedy, and that Larsen has more momentum and a better chance of making a dent.Read More→

IN THE NEWSOctober 4, 2026Democratic Party Runs More Than 60 Military-Intelligence Candidates for CongressWorld Socialist Web Site (WSWS)Part four of a WSWS series on Democratic congressional candidates with military and intelligence backgrounds. The article profiles Larsen as the Democratic candidate in Utah's heavily Republican 4th District, running against first-term Rep. Mike Kennedy, and cites his two Iraq deployments with the Marines: the initial push into Baghdad with 3rd Battalion, 4th Marines and the Battle of Husaybah with 3rd Battalion, 7th Marines. It also notes his career in IT and his outreach to the district's 30,000 veterans.Campaign note: The World Socialist Web Site is a socialist publication. Jonny Larsen is a Blue Dog Democrat and a social democrat. He is not affiliated with, and does not identify with, the Democratic Socialists of America (DSA) or any socialist party or organization. Listing this coverage is not an endorsement of the publication or its views.Read More→

IN THE NEWSOctober 7, 20262026 General Election Voter Guide: U.S. House District 4Utah News DispatchUtah News Dispatch's voter guide to the 4th District, with candidates' answers in their own words. Larsen answers all four questions: the Great Salt Lake and water, the Iran War and affordability, energy, and representing every Utahn in the district. Kennedy did not provide a response to any of them.Read More→

IN THE NEWSOctober 7, 2026New Map, Open Seat: Utah's 4th District Candidates to DebateDeseret NewsThe Deseret News preview of the race for the newly drawn 4th District, which now takes in Tooele, Millard, Sanpete, Juab and Sevier counties and parts of Salt Lake and Utah counties. It profiles Larsen as a Marine infantry rifleman from 2000 to 2004 and a cancer survivor whose campaign centers on housing and cost of living, public lands, data centers and health care.Read More→

IN THE NEWSOctober 8, 2026Candidates Clash Over Iran War, Gas Prices in Utah 4th District DebateKSL.comKSL's recap of the debate at Snow College's Eccles Performing Arts Center. Larsen makes direct appeals to Republican voters as a moderate "blue dog" Democrat, calls out Kennedy for voting against resolutions to limit the president's war powers, and closes by asking voters whether they want a blue dog or a lapdog to this administration. Afterward, he says he'll keep doing what he has done all along: boots on the ground, meeting voters so they feel heard.Read More→

IN THE NEWSOctober 8, 2026Candidates Clash in Utah's Fourth Congressional District DebateFOX 13 News UtahFOX 13's debate recap. Larsen, who did two combat tours, calls for ending the Iran War, says public lands must remain in public hands, and backs a moratorium on data centers until they can work for everyone, saying district voters are upset and not being listened to. He closes by asking Republicans to cross over and vote for a moderate Democrat.Read More→

IN THE NEWSOctober 8, 2026KSL Truth Test: Fact-Checking Debate Claims in Utah's 4th Congressional DistrictKSL.comThe KSL Investigators fact-check both candidates. Larsen's claim that Kennedy voted against war powers resolutions on Iran six times is rated true. Kennedy's claim about Iran's missile range is rated unproven, and his BlackRock claim both true and false. KSL also rates Larsen's $650,000 Utah County home-price figure false, finding medians of $523,000 for all housing and $605,000 for single-family homes.Read More→

IN THE NEWSOctober 8, 2026Mike Kennedy, Jonny Larsen Spar Over Gas Prices and Iran in Utah 4th District DebateKUER 90.1KUER's recap of the debate in a district the new map tripled in size. Larsen calls the Iran War illegal and says Kennedy failed his duty as a congressman to end it, backs better irrigation so conserved water can reach the Great Salt Lake, says public lands must remain in public hands, and closes by asking Republicans to put party aside and vote for someone who wants government to work together.Read More→

IN THE NEWSOctober 8, 2026North Valley Chief Says ICE Ride-Along Went Beyond What He Expected, Department Reevaluating AgreementSanpete MessengerThe Messenger's in-depth report on the Sept. 30 ICE operation in Moroni, built on an hour-long interview with North Valley Police Chief Steve Gray, who says the ride-along went beyond what he expected and that his department is reevaluating its 287(g) agreement with ICE. Larsen, the Democratic candidate for Utah's 4th District, which includes Sanpete County, calls the current national approach to immigration enforcement a disgrace. He says earlier administrations deported large numbers of people humanely and constitutionally, and warns of the economic toll on communities where immigrant workers are part of the labor force.Read More→

IN THE NEWSOctober 9, 2026In Debate, Utah Rep. Kennedy Says He's 'Just Getting Started' While Dem Calls Him a 'Lap Dog'Utah News DispatchUtah News Dispatch's debate recap leads with Larsen's closing question to voters: do they want a "blue dog" or a lap dog to the Trump administration? It covers his call to end the Iran War to bring fuel prices down, his push to protect public lands and rural groundwater from mining and drilling, and his criticism of the ICE detentions at the Moroni turkey plant in Sanpete County. The story was also republished by the Daily Herald, News From The States and PoliticIt.Read More→

IN THE NEWSOctober 9, 2026Rep. Mike Kennedy and Veteran Jonny Larsen Debate Iran War and Affordability in Fight for 4th Congressional DistrictThe Salt Lake TribuneThe Tribune's recap of the only televised debate in the race, at Snow College in Ephraim. Larsen, a Marine Corps combat veteran, says Kennedy gave up his constitutional duty by backing the Iran War without congressional approval, and calls for ending it to bring gas prices down. A cancer survivor treated through the VA, he makes the case for that kind of care for every American, defends federal public lands and the PILT payments rural counties rely on, and calls ICE raids "very sinister."Read More→
